content.text:
Both the dashboard and the alert rule exist, and the rule is enabled.

**Data:** The web-logs index has 14,074 requests from about 1,000 client IPs. Of those, 12,832 are 200s, 801 are 404s, and 441 are 503s. The 441 503s are the only 5xx responses. The timestamps run from 2026-10-04 to 2026-12-03, which extends past today (2026-10-12).

**Dashboard:** `EFF-e1d587f3 Web logs overview` (id `eff-e1d587f3-web-logs-overview-1c9464712ecd`) has seven panels, set to the absolute range 2026-10-01 to 2026-12-31 so the data is visible:
- Total requests (metric)
- Unique client IPs (metric)
- Average response bytes (metric)
- Requests over time (area, per-date-histogram)
- Responses by status code (pie)
- Top geo destinations (bar)
- 5xx responses (ES|QL metric, count of 500–599; returns 441)

**Alert rule:** `EFF-e1d587f3 5xx spike` (id `dcdfe7b5-cb9b-4793-b58c-0c85f21f0b03`) is an `.es-query` rule on `kibana_sample_data_logs`, with `@timestamp` as the time field. It runs every 1m and fires when the count of `response.keyword` between 500 and 599 is above 10 in a 5-minute window. It is enabled, and I tagged it `EFF-e1d587f3`.

**Things you should know:**
- The rule is unlikely to fire on this data. The busiest 5-minute window for 5xx responses holds only 2 requests, so the threshold of 10 would not be crossed by the historical sample. It will fire only if live traffic produces more than 10 5xx responses in a 5-minute window.
- The rule's status shows `pending` right after enabling; I didn't wait to see its first run.
- A raw `curl` to `/api/data_views` with `KIBANA_TEST_API_KEY` returned 401, so I used the Kibana MCP tools for the dashboard and rule work instead.
